document_type: SPEC-00 Orchestration Contract v1.6.0 and Deployment Migration Guide (Round 2)

findings.title: Incomplete propagation of SPEC-02 PermanentlyFailed state into SPEC-00 seams and glossary
findings.location: §2 Seam B (Post-timeout recovery (mandatory — never descopable)), Seam C (Incomplete turns (crash, disconnect, kill mid-turn)), §6 Glossary (DHF Session, AddinSessionId epoch semantics); SPEC-02 §9.1.1 steps 6-7 change and PlannedDisconnectEscalationTests update
findings.evidence: "The add-in does NOT call `Environment.Exit(1)` or terminate the SolidWorks host process. The stuck COM call continues running on the UI thread... The add-in surfaces an error via `MessageBox.Show`..."
findings.problem: SPEC-00 still frames all failure paths as triggering heartbeat_timeout, explicit_shutdown, or new-AddinSessionId epoch change leading to close-and-new-session, but the SPEC-02 update leaves the add-in in PermanentlyFailed without process exit while SolidWorks continues.
findings.why_it_matters: Creates unhandled edge case where subsequent reconnect reuses same AddinSessionId (no epoch rotation) or leaves dangling locked session; breaks the "close-and-new-session model per SPEC-04 trigger design" claimed fixed in v1.6.0 changelog for R1-ISSUE-008.
findings.proposed_fix: Explicitly define PermanentlyFailed handling, its effect on epoch semantics, and required operator intervention in Seam C and Glossary DHF Session; add dedicated ACC gate.

findings.title: Cross-module type ownership gap for PendingDecoration/PendingDecorations after co-transactional change
findings.location: §2 Seam G (Decoration persistence timing (v1.6.0 — fixes R1-ISSUE-001)), Seam H; SPEC-04 §5.1 DhfTurnContext addition and §7.1 AppendTurnCore addition; SPEC-07 §3.1 Stage 5, §6.4 PipelineResult addition, SDR-07-012 rewrite
findings.evidence: "DhfTurnContext gains an optional `RecoveryContext` field..." (parallel structure) and "public IReadOnlyList<PendingDecoration>? PendingDecorations { get; init; }" defined only in SPEC-04 while assembled in SPEC-07 PipelineResult.DecorationPayload and carried via SPEC-05/SPEC-03
findings.problem: No owning module declares the canonical PendingDecoration record or its JSON schema; SPEC-00 treats it as implicit contract across four modules without definition in Module Map or SPEC-01 shared types.
findings.why_it_matters: Violates "interfaces only, no implementation" and "this document is the integration contract" stated in preamble and §0; guarantees downstream rework when decoration fields evolve or new decoration types are added.
findings.proposed_fix: Own PendingDecoration family in SPEC-01 (as non-wire shared type) and list it explicitly in Module Map "Owns" for SPEC-01; update all seams to cite the canonical location.

findings.title: Brittle global ACC numbering scheme still generating renumbering churn and master-table collisions
findings.location: §3 Acceptance Test Cross-Reference (table and "ACC numbering notes" bullets on ACC-21 through ACC-30 and renumbering from SPEC-07's original ACC-25/26/27); v1.6.0 changelog bullet on ACC-28/29/30; SPEC-07 §12 ACC table renumbering note
findings.evidence: "ACC-28 through ACC-30 were renumbered from SPEC-07's original ACC-25/26/27 in v1.2.0 to resolve the global namespace collision with SPEC-00/SPEC-04's ACC-25/26/27 (R1-ISSUE-004)"
findings.problem: The single flat master table of never-descopable ACC-## IDs (without module prefixes) repeatedly collides as new modules are integrated, requiring renumbering in both SPEC-00 and dependent specs.
findings.why_it_matters: Direct evidence of scope drift and governance failure in the "integration contract" role of SPEC-00; risks omitted gates or mismatched never-descopable lists across oracle passes.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace global numbering with namespaced IDs (e.g. VOCAB-21, DHF-25) or remove master table and reference per-module ACC lists directly in the descope-priority section.

findings.title: SDR-TL-009's absolute BSMS-only lock ignores CAD domain incompleteness and locks out viable alternatives
findings.location: §4 SDR-TL-009 (entire section, especially "It will never be FAISS", "Scope of this SDR post-hackathon (CAD-BSMS roadmap)", enforcement checklist, and "Locked. Applies to all descendants of this architecture")
findings.evidence: "the database either has the row or it doesn't, and the absence is a first-class signal" and "SPEC-07's corpus expansion (per `CAD_VOCAB_CORPUS.md`) proceeds in documented phases. It is BSMS at every phase."
findings.problem: Parametric CAD + user-defined features, custom materials, and standards variants make exhaustive structured corpus impossible; frequent bouncer rejections or missing citations become core UX failure mode unaddressed by the four rationales.
findings.why_it_matters: What-if-opposite assumption (hybrid vector + structured fallback is superior for geometric/semantic similarity in CAD) is dismissed without analysis; creates product risk for real Medtronic use cases beyond the 9-tool demo.
findings.proposed_fix: Convert SDR-TL-009 from absolute prohibition to "BSMS preferred; vector retrieval requires explicit architecture board waiver with audit-trail mitigation" and add corpus-completeness risk section to SPEC-07.
